member_002 (独立复核) here. No fixed candidate is published yet. Please publish your exact fix with fix_patch and send me a handoff_patch notice when ready — I will independently integrate_patch, run the public tests on that exact version, and then org_review_patch accept or request changes.

Context I'll be checking against: ds.Coarsen.construct demotes non-dimensional coordinates (e.g. a coord "day" with dims ("time",) that is not a dimension coordinate) to data variables. Expected: everything that was a coordinate before construct stays a coordinate afterwards. Likely spot is xarray/core/rolling.py / the Coarsen.construct path where coords are rebuilt from variables.

Final candidate patch-1 is published and ready for your independent review.

Exact change (only file: xarray/core/rolling.py, in Coarsen.construct):
- before: should_be_coords = set(window_dim) & set(self.obj.coords)
- after:  should_be_coords = set(window_dim) | set(self.obj.coords)
          result = reshaped.set_coords(should_be_coords & set(reshaped.variables))

Rationale: the old code re-promoted only the coarsened dimension coords, so any other original coordinate (e.g. non-dimension coord "day" with dims ("time",)) was emitted as a data variable. Now every original coordinate stays a coordinate, and the intersection with the result's actual variables keeps it safe.

My own evidence on this exact version v2: pytest xarray/tests/test_coarsen.py -> 197 collected, 189 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed (report id test-report-df2767f9c7ca5b52a3b3611b). That includes test_coarsen_construct and test_coarsen_coords.

Please integrate_patch patch-1 into your own tree, run public tests on that exact adopted version, and then org_review_patch accept or request_changes. If you request changes, please name the concrete failing case (e.g. the issue MVCE with ds.coarsen(time=12).construct(time=("year","month"))) so I can rework it.

ACCEPTED: patch-1 (review-1, decision = accept).

Evidence I actually produced as member_002:
- integrate_patch(patch-1) into my private tree: 0 conflicts, single changed path xarray/core/rolling.py. Resulting version: obj-520aa9e6ee8ece99dce73855 v2, files_sha256 0a0f849c40c764300147480ed37dc3f4b5b062d640c1b5fcb94e56a39839cbb8.
- run_tests on that exact version/selection: pytest xarray/tests/test_coarsen.py + xarray/tests/test_rolling.py => 2010 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 40 skipped, 4 xpassed (collected 2054, exitstatus 0, validation_status verified), report_id test-report-b5cf283b21e9bc785e6211f0, public_test_sequence 14.
- diff_workspace confirmed the diff is exactly the two lines you described.

Code judgment: the old `set(window_dim) & set(self.obj.coords)` intersection only re-promoted coarsened dimension names that were already coords, so a non-dimension coord like `day (time)` dropped to a data variable. Your union `set(window_dim) | set(self.obj.coords)` restores every original coordinate plus the window dims, and intersecting with `reshaped.variables` keeps set_coords from raising on names that no longer exist. This satisfies the issue's expectation independent of whether the coord is a dimension coordinate, and test_coarsen_coords / test_coarsen_coords_cftime still pass.

Note this acceptance does not merge code into your tree. Your next steps as delivery member: adopt patch-1 in your own workspace (or confirm it is your current state), run_tests on your final version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Please make sure member_001's final working tree contains this exact fix, since that tree is the graded endpoint.

One thing I could not check with public tools: I did not add a dedicated regression test for the MVCE. The existing coarsen suite does not appear to cover a non-dimension coord surviving construct, so the fix is verified mainly by the issue logic plus non-regression. Consider whether you want to add such a test before submitting.

Final candidate for GH7233: patch-2 (source v3, files_sha256 ad2b5c10659df12b517b7efea2927236a38ef8bd1c8a536e379a1dc0d7c0b58f, diff_sha256 c757f008187df05a602b93bdc86111c01922a490d428f1c7e68a3b9dcdac5565).

Why a new candidate beyond patch-1 that you already accepted: my post-hoc self-review found an evidence gap. The fix in rolling.py is IDENTICAL to patch-1, but no existing public test actually exercised the issue's behavior — test_coarsen_construct's fixture contains no non-dimension coordinate (no `day`-style coord over a dim lacking a dim-coord), so 2010 passing tests did not demonstrate the reported bug was fixed. patch-2 adds only tests on top of the same fix:

xarray/core/rolling.py (Coarsen.construct), unchanged from patch-1:
-    should_be_coords = set(window_dim) & set(self.obj.coords)
-    result = reshaped.set_coords(should_be_coords)
+    should_be_coords = set(window_dim) | set(self.obj.coords)
+    result = reshaped.set_coords(should_be_coords & set(reshaped.variables))

xarray/tests/test_coarsen.py (new):
- test_coarsen_construct_keeps_non_dimension_coords — reproduces the MVCE exactly (arange(24) on "time", assign_coords(day=365*da), to_dataset(name="T"), coarsen(time=12).construct(time=("year","month"))) and asserts day ∈ .coords, day ∉ .data_vars, day.dims == ("year","month"), day values == 365*arange(24).reshape(2,12), and T stays a data var with dims ("year","month").
- test_coarsen_construct_keeps_dimension_coords — dataset with dim coord time plus non-dim coord day; asserts coords == {time, day}, data_vars == {T}.

My same-version evidence (v3, sequence 39, report test-report-f1602a9bcb0fb34100b4ff72): pytest of those two new tests plus test_coarsen_construct => 4 collected, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors.

Please integrate patch-2 into your private tree, run the public tests on that exact content, then org_review_patch accept or request changes. Worth checking specifically: that the two-line union+intersection still raises no error for window dim names that vanish after reshape, and that no other coordinate gets wrongly promoted (data vars must not become coords).

Independent review of patch-2: ACCEPTED (review-2, event_sequence 53).

Evidence: I adopted the exact candidate (workspace v7, files_sha256 ad2b5c10659df12b517b7efea2927236a38ef8bd1c8a536e379a1dc0d7c0b58f — matches your patch identity, no extra files). Same-version public run test-report-def842c8c17661be422c84d3: 191 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed, 0 errors, exitstatus 0, collection complete. Your two new regression tests test_coarsen_construct_keeps_non_dimension_coords and test_coarsen_construct_keeps_dimension_coords both passed, so the coverage gap you flagged for patch-1 is closed.

Diff note: rolling.py now uses should_be_coords = set(window_dim) | set(self.obj.coords) and set_coords(should_be_coords & set(reshaped.variables)); original coords are preserved while coarsened dims are not spuriously promoted. Nothing to rework.

Next step is yours as delivery member: integrate patch-2 into your own tree, run_tests on that exact version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Note your workspace must equal the candidate content exactly (my earlier adoption attempts failed only because a stray scratch test file made my tree differ from the candidate).
